News.title: I’m putting my head in the sand until next election – Labour must U-turn on absurd inheritance tax, Jeremy Clarkson says
News.content:
TAX FURY I’m putting my head in the sand until next election – Labour must U-turn on absurd inheritance tax, Jeremy Clarkson says

JEREMY Clarkson has launched a furious attack on Labour’s inheritance tax stance, claiming he’ll “put his head in the sand” until the next election.

The former Top Gear star joked he’d “make like an ostrich” as he railed against what he called an “absurd tax on the dead”.





Writing in his column for The Times, Clarkson fumed: “That’s my clever plan: hang on till the Labourites have gone.”

The outspoken presenter said he was left grappling with the “unbelievably complicated” business of dying, including how to pass on his wealth.

Clarkson joked he had considered everything from setting up trusts to handing over his fortune early.

He pointed to the seven-year rule on gifts, which can make them tax-free if the giver lives long enough, as one of the hurdles.



The TV farmer also took a tongue-in-cheek swipe at his closest pals while discussing his will.

He quipped: “You have to leave some people 20p so they don’t think you forgot about them.

“And I have James May to worry about. Obviously, I have to leave him something, but it needs to be something he’d find irritating. One of my cows, for example.

He then joked that Richard Hammond would get all his trousers.



Clarkson’s rant follows Sir Keir Starmer watering down his inheritance tax raid on farmers after months of angry protests.

The PM quietly announced in December last year that the threshold at which the levy applies will rise from £1m to £2.5m.

It will enable spouses to pass on £5m worth of agricultural assets between them before being hit by inheritance tax.



The partial U-turn follows 14 months of enraged protests, led by the Clarkson’s Farm star himself.

Clearly the minor reforms were not enough for Clarkson, who doubled down on his attack and warned the tax could have grim consequences for families across Britain.

He went on to paint a bleak picture of how the tax could even affect his final moments.

Clarkson said that he had a scenario in mind in which he might suffer some kind of medical issue and “become a cabbage.”

He warned that if his family followed his wishes and “pull the plug”, they could be slapped with a “whopping tax bill,” but dodging it might mean keeping him alive.



If they waited until Starmer and Reeves had gone, they would not face that situation, he added.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

In a dark joke, he said he may need to rewrite his will to insist life support is kept on until “the Labourites are out of Downing Street”.

Taking a swipe at Chancellor Rachel Reeves, Clarkson said the policy could leave NHS hospitals “full of people on fantastically expensive life support machines” because families can’t afford to let them die.

News.title: Ukrainians forced to flee trains from deadly Russian drones after Putin hit maternity hospital in night of ‘pure terror’
News.content:
THIS is the harrowing moment scores of Ukrainians are evacuated from a packed train amid Russian strikes with Iranian-made Shahed drones.

Terrifying footage shows civilians fleeing multiple carriages in anticipation of deadly drone attacks in the early hours of this morning.





Wrapped in woollen blankets, they are seen running away from the tracks after their journey from the city of Kryvyi Rih to Kyiv was severely disrupted.

Up above, witness said a drone could be heard piercing the sky above as a Ukrainian army interceptor followed behind.

In addition to attacking Ukraine‘s energy infrastructure, Russia has been intensifying strikes on the country’s rail lines – only adding to Putin’s attacks on civilians.

Ukraine‘s public railway company, Ukrzaliznytsia, has reported that engine wagons, freight cars and railway maintenance equipment have come under increased Russian fire since early March.

More frequent Russian attacks on bridges and rail yards have also been recorded.

This comes less than a week after a 61-year-old passenger was killed when a Russian drone struck a commuter train in the Kharkiv region, a few miles from the Russian border.

This morning‘s attacks follow a night of “pure terror” unleashed by Russia, in which at least five people were killed and another 16 injured, including a child.



A wave of attacks saw some 273 drones deployed on a maternity hospital in the Black Sea port city of Odesa and a school in Kramatorsk.

Ihor Shpak, the hospital’s chief doctor, said that a powerful explosion had ripped through the building, destroying the roof, connecting structures between the fourth and third floors, and some hospital wards.

Medics managed to evacuate 22 newborns, including twins who were on ventilator support, and 32 other patients to the shelter just before the attack, he said.

Olena Kudriashova, an Odesa resident, said she was scared when Shahed drones were flying towards her house.

“On the right, ⁠on the left, at the front, and at the back, windows and doors were smashed,” she said.



“Our little window survived, and we’re so happy we made it through the night,

Gas production facilities, port infrastructure and apartment blocks were also struck as at least two dozen drones bypassed Ukrainian defences.

“Last night, the Russians massively attacked Odessa,” Volodymyr Zelensky wrote.

“No military sense, this is pure terror against ordinary civilian life. There were more than 60 strike drones in this attack on the city. Unfortunately, there is a lot of damage.

“Among the objects that were affected are a maternity hospital, ordinary residential buildings, enterprises, port and critical infrastructure.”



RECOMMENDED STORIES

While Russia continued to pound civilian areas, the Ukrainian military has intensified drone attacks on oil and fuel export infrastructure.

Just this month, it hit all three ⁠of Russia’s major western ​oil ⁠export ports, including Novorossiysk on the Black Sea and Primorsk and Ust-Luga on the ⁠Baltic Sea.

News.title: Horror injuries suffered by Air Canada stewardess who was thrown 320ft out of plane in LaGuardia crash revealed
News.content:
A VETERAN flight attendant who was violently flung from a crashing plane has been pictured in her hospital bed for the first time.

Air Canada crew member, Solange Tremblay, was hurled more than 320 feet across the runway when Jazz flight 8646 smashed into a fire truck at New York’s LaGuardia Airport on the night of March 22.





The horror impact reportedly catapulted the stewardess from the wreckage, leaving rescuers to discover her lying on the tarmac – still strapped into her jump seat.

Her daughter Sarah Lepine described the terrifying moment in a GoFundMe appeal set up to help with her mum’s medical treatment.

She wrote: “During the crash she was… ejected over 320 feet from the wreckage. She was found still strapped in her jump seat lying on the tarmac.”

Lepine said the long-serving flight attendant suffered catastrophic injuries in the violent crash.

“My mother’s injuries include two shattered legs (open fractures) requiring multiple surgeries where metal plates are needed to repair the damage done to her legs,” she added.

“She sustained a fractured spine where she continues to wait and see if surgery is required. Furthermore, she requires skin graphs to repair the missing flesh she lost on her legs while sliding down the tarmac.”

“She has even received a blood transfusion due to complications from her first surgery.”



Despite her devastating injuries, Lepine said her mum surviving the crash was “a total miracle”.

“I’m still trying to understand how all this happened, but she definitely has a guardian angel watching over her,” she told Canadian news station TVA Nouvelles.

Two pilots – Antoine Forest from Quebec and Mackenzie Gunther – were killed in the crash when the CRJ-900 jet, carrying 72 passengers and four crew members from Montreal, slammed into a Port Authority fire truck crossing the runway.

More than 40 people were injured in the disaster, which witnesses said ended with a deafening “boom” as the aircraft’s nose was crushed in the impact.

Passengers said the pilots likely prevented an even greater tragedy as the jet skidded along the runway after the impact.



“I feel terrible about the pilots and I think they are honestly heroes,” passenger Joe Capio told The U.S. Sun. “The pilots greeted us and were very nice. They saved everybody on that plane.”

Another passenger, Rebecca Liquori, said the aircraft jolted violently moments before the crash.

“It was like the plane jolted and you heard the pilot try to brake trying to prevent the collision,” she said. “As you heard the brake, a couple seconds later it was just a very loud boom.”

The CRJ-900 jet had been carrying 72 passengers and four crew members from Montreal when it slammed into a Port Authority fire truck crossing the runway, leaving the nose of the aircraft mangled and more than 40 people injured.

Security camera footage later showed the fire truck with flashing lights crossing directly into the plane’s path just seconds before the collision, sending the vehicle tumbling on impact.



Aviation safety experts described Tremblay’s survival as “remarkable,” noting the jump seat she was strapped into is built to withstand extreme forces and protect crew during crashes.

LaGuardia Airport was shut down while emergency crews responded and investigators examined the scene, reopening the following afternoon with reduced capacity.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the investigation could take months and urged passengers to always keep their seatbelts fastened.

“Seeing what happened at the crash site is a reminder that seatbelts save lives – whether on a plane or in a car,” he said.

News.title: Bomb shelter raves, ‘death stickers’ & the burning village reduced to a crater… brutality of life in war-scorched Israel
News.content:
MILLIONS of Israelis will once again spend today running to air raid shelters as the latest barrage of Iranian ballistic missiles head their way at 10,000mph.

For them, the end of war can’t come soon enough.





The message I heard again and again during the two weeks I have just spent reporting from Israel was: “We just want to live in peace.”

But the dozens of people I spoke to, including the President, young liberals in cosmopolitan Tel Aviv and Israeli Arabs, also kept telling me: “To achieve peace, we have to go to war.”

Israel is a country that has been permanently at war for years now, against Hamas, Hezbollah and now Iran.



It is impossible to ignore the sights and sounds of war wherever you go, the most obvious being the air raid sirens.

Every day mobile phones erupt in an ear-splitting alarm as a message pops up: “Alerts are expected in a few minutes. Find the best protection around.”

A short time later a more urgent message arrives with yet another screech warning of rocket and missile fire and an instruction to take shelter.

Everyone obeys it, unlike in Ukraine where I found while reporting on the war there that it tends to be a 50-50 split between those who take shelter and those who carry on regardless.



In Israel, everyone is aware that the threat of Iran’s ballistic missiles such as the Khorramshahr-4 with its 1,800kg war head far outweigh anything Hamas or Hezbollah have in their arsenal.

As well as the phone alerts, the eerie wail of sirens which echo through now-deserted streets is the final warning for anyone not already underground.

The shelters themselves vary. Some are dusty basements which feel like they have no other use while others are better equipped.

One I went into had table tennis, pool and air hockey tables.

There are three types of shelters.



Private ones in people’s homes are known as Mamads. Built from reinforced concrete, they have been mandatory in all houses built since 1991.

Shared ones on a specific floor of a building are called Mamaks while in buildings such as hotels and institutions they are called Mamachs.

To qualify as a shelter they all have to meet specific standards set down by the Home Front Command, charged with protecting the public in times of war.

There are apps to help people locate them including navigation app Waze which has a feature to direct people to the nearest one.

In the residential areas the shelters have a community feel with people catching up with neighbours they haven’t seen for a while.



One hosted a pop-up techno nightclub and a couple getting married decided to say their vows underground.

One night we witnessed a couple entertain their shelter with an impromptu acrobatics display.



On another occasion, I got chatting with a young couple, dressed for a night out, who had both lived in London.

I asked them how long they had been together and they giggled as they revealed it was their first date.

The all clear sounded soon after and I never did get to find out if there was a second date.

As you travel around Israel it’s impossible to ignore the events of the last few years.

Service stations, roundabouts and lampposts are covered in thousands of stickers, each with the name and picture of someone killed in Israel’s wars.



They also include a QR code which takes you to their own personal website with page after page telling their life story in detail.

Another indication of a society at war is the number of young men and women wandering around Civvy Street with an M16 assault rifle slung over their shoulder.

At breakfast in one hotel I saw a dad sporting peyote, the two long curls of hair common to some Jewish sects, carrying his standard issue army rifle as he inspected the buffet with his young son at his side. A handgun poked out of his trouser pocket.

It reflects a society-wide level of military readiness which has long been part of Israel’s survival DNA.

Another sound heard, almost daily, is the boom of the country’s sophisticated air defences as they take out another missile.



Most of the incoming fire is intercepted, but not all.

I visited a Bedouin village in the north where a missile had struck, damaging 300 homes and injuring more than 50.



The blast had left trees blackened and with no leaves, although there was a metal hut stuck in the upper branches after it had been hurled across garden.

President Herzog also attended the scene and after inspecting the blast crater told me: “This shows we need to be doing what we are doing to Iran.

“There are two alternatives – one is terror, hate, bloodshed endlessly by the empire of evil from Tehran.

“And the other is a coalition of nations and peoples, Muslims, Jews and Christians who seek peace.”

Those sentiments were echoed by many I spoke to, including younger men and women who would never dream of voting for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, a polarising figure at home and abroad.



Like young adults everywhere with their whole lives ahead of them they just want peace, but feel that is impossible without taking on Iran first.

But they are also exhausted by constant war and some wonder if these seemingly never-ending conflicts is the right way to do achieve that peace.

Yet, they also think, if Iran was as close to getting a nuclear weapon as the politicians claim what other option did Israel have?

Noga, 24, a student said: “This is a war that was likely inevitable and we are fortunate that Donald Trump was willing to take such action against Iran.



“My concern is that this may prove to be just another round of conflict, rather than the last.”

Her friend Romi, 25, also a student, added: “It’s been difficult living in a country at war for the past two and a half years.

“The home front is exhausted, constantly running to bomb shelters and unable to maintain any routine or stability.

“At the same time I worry that relying on war as a solution only prolongs the conflict.”



And Nadav, 26, a legal assistant, said: “Whatever one thinks of Netanyahu, there is no doubt that Israel ultimately had to confront Iran. This has been a looming threat for years.”

While the politicians and public debate the rights and wrongs, the IDF executes its battle plans with ruthless efficiency.

In the north, it is adopting the same tactics to destroy Hezbollah as it did against Hamas in Gaza.

Some of the villages in southern Lebanon, where the Iran-funded terror group has been based for decades, now resemble the destroyed towns of Gaza.

After entering Israel at its southern border with Egypt, myself and Sun photographer Dan Charity drove around 350 miles to the country’s most northerly town of Metula.



From there it is possible to look into southern Lebanon and see those destroyed houses with the naked eye.

Three Divisions of the IDF – the 91st “Galilee” Regional Division, the 146th Reserve Division and the 36th Division – are now either based inside Lebanon or have carried out targeted raids there.

Airstrikes are also hitting the capital of Beirut, especially the southern suburbs of Dahieh where Hezbollah has its biggest presence.



Around 1,000 people have now been killed in Lebanon since Hezbollah joined the war in support of Iran on day two.

Critics accuse Israel of being a warmongering bully because of the overwhelming military force it employs against its enemies.

But those sentiments won’t sway the government or the IDF in their efforts to establish a Hezbollah-free buffer zone in the south.

Governments go to war, not people. In Israel many ordinary people do want peace, but feel the only way to achieve that is to kill the people trying to kill them.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

That is hard to stomach for people living in a conflict-free countries.



But another common message I heard during my time in Israel, often said with a shrug, was: “That’s the Middle East for you.”

News.title: Fears another Brit killed by ‘war zone’ stomach bug as widow says husband died in same holiday outbreak as SIX others
News.content:
A GRIEVING widow fears her ex-Royal Navy husband died after being struck down with the same stomach bug that killed six Brits in Cape Verde.

A deadly outbreak ripped through luxury resorts in the holiday hotspot last year leaving another 1,500 tourists ill.





Now, a woman from County Durham believes her retired firefighter partner, 52, was also struck down by the same illness on August 11.

The dad-of-two became unwell during a week-long trip with his wife, daughter and her boyfriend after they arrived for the £6,500 all-inclusive stay at the five-star Riu Palace Santa Maria on the island of Sal, lawyers say.

His death comes as a bombshell legal battle unfolds over the deadly gastric illness outbreak.



The highly contagious bacterial infection Shigella can cause potentially life-threatening dysentery

The latest victim’s devastated wife said his illness sounded like “a carbon copy” of other cases.

She said he battled symptoms for 12 weeks before suffering multi-organ failure and dying on November 2.

Paying tribute, she said: “We’re still in complete shock over his death. My husband was my soulmate and an absolutely wonderful, loving and caring dad.



“We never imagined that going on what we thought would be an enjoyable holiday would lead to such traumatic events unfolding.

“I’d do anything to turn the clock back, but I know nothing can undo what’s happened and how our family will never be the same again.

“However, I wouldn’t want anyone else to suffer the same experience. People need to be aware of the issues hundreds of holidaymakers to Cape Verde are facing.”

The family had visited the same resort the previous year to celebrate his retirement and enjoyed it so much they returned.

But his wife said they were shocked by what they found when they arrived the second time.



She said: “We’d been to the resort the year before to celebrate my husband’s retirement and enjoyed it so much we booked again to return.

“However, as soon as we arrived the second time, we couldn’t believe how much it appeared to have changed from our previous holiday.

“We didn’t expect the poor standards we experienced, especially for the money we paid.

“When my husband fell ill, he tried to continue but the holiday was ruined. Even more worrying was how his symptoms continued to persist once we got home.

“He tried to carry on but it was obvious he wasn’t himself and was still suffering.”



On the third day of the trip he began vomiting and suffering diarrhoea and loss of appetite.

He was the only member of the group to become ill.

But his symptoms did not improve after the family returned home on August 18.

Instead, he spent two months housebound – needing the toilet up to 15 times a day and unable to eat properly.

His stomach and legs became severely swollen while he rapidly lost weight.



After visiting his GP on October 12 he was told to return in two weeks if he still felt unwell.

When he went back on October 27 he was rushed to A&E, where doctors drained a large amount of fluid from his abdomen.

Despite treatment, he died six days later.

His death came just over a week before another British tourist, Mark Ashley, died on November 12 after falling ill during a stay at the same resort.



Doctors initially recorded his cause of death as multi-organ failure and alcohol-related liver disease.

His wife Emma, 55, said the family were in “complete shock”.

She said: “We went to Cape Verde expecting a relaxing break, but Mark became violently ill and never recovered…The last couple of months have been unbearable, and our family will never be the same again.”



Another dad-of-two from Chester also died days earlier after visiting a RIU hotel on a different island.

Among the other victims was 64-year-old Elena Walsh, who fell ill during a £5,000 “trip of a lifetime” with her family.

She began suffering sickness, diarrhoea and sweating on August 8 while staying at a five-star resort.

The mum was taken to a clinic before being rushed to hospital when her condition worsened.

She died two days later.



Heartbroken husband Patrick said the family had grave concerns about hygiene standards at the hotel.

He claimed food was often served lukewarm and not properly cooked while medical care was “chaotic” before her death.

Another victim, Karen Pooley, 64, from Lydney, Gloucestershire, also died after developing sickness and diarrhoea during a stay at the RIU Funana resort.

The mum-of-two was taken to a local clinic before being airlifted to intensive care in Tenerife.

She died five days later.



Her cause of death was listed as multi-organ failure, sepsis, cardiac arrest and a broken left leg after she slipped on water at the hotel.

Her husband Andy, 62, said the family had been left “utterly heartbroken”.

He said: “We’re devastated and struggling to understand how she went on holiday and never came home.”

Two other British tourists have also died after falling ill following trips to Cape Verde since 2023.

Jane Pressley, 62, from Gainsborough, died in January 2023 after becoming sick while staying at the Riu Palace Hotel in Santa Maria.



A man in his 60s from Watford also died in November 2024 after suffering a gastric illness.

Researchers investigating the outbreak collected 156 samples from drinking water, fresh food, food preparation surfaces and irrigation systems across the islands.

Shigella bacteria were discovered in irrigation water used to wash produce as well as on some imported foods.

The UK Health Security Agency recorded 137 cases of the infection between October and December, with around 80 per cent of patients having recently travelled to Cape Verde.

In December, the Foreign Office issued a warning to British travellers about the outbreak.



Serious injury lawyer Jatinder Paul, from Irwin Mitchell, said the number of holidaymakers becoming ill was “truly staggering”.

He said: “Each case isn’t a statistic; it’s a human story of how lives have been turned upside down.”

He urged travellers heading to Cape Verde to ensure meals are “fully cooked, steaming hot”, choose fruit they can peel and avoid raw vegetables or salads.

Several group legal actions are now expected to reach the High Court.

The first case – involving 300 holidaymakers who fell ill after staying at a RIU resort in 2022 – is due to be heard soon.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

TUI and RIU Hotels & Resorts previously said they were “deeply saddened” by the deaths and offered their “heartfelt condolences to the families affected”.

The Sun has approached both companies for comment.

News.title: Locals at war with looming ‘eyesore’ caravan park that ‘lights up like Blackpool & means they can’t use their HOT TUBS’
News.content:
LIFE'S A PITCH Locals at war with looming ‘eyesore’ caravan park that ‘lights up like Blackpool & means they can’t use their HOT TUBS’

FURIOUS residents have accused an “eyesore” holiday park of ruining their privacy and wiping £100,000 off the value of their homes.

Locals living in Luney Barton near St Austell, Cornwall, have moaned they are now living in the shadow of dozens of static caravans.





They no longer feel comfortable spending evenings in the garden and even close the curtains when indoors because they feel so overlooked.

Residents have been locked in a battle with Cornwall Council for the last three years after the site was significantly expanded.



The expansion saw new static caravans and infrastructure including roads and new concrete bases built for holidaymakers.

Homeowners claim the caravans have been placed in a different part of the site to the initial agreement in a historic application.

But planning officials have insisted the new development does not “breach planning control”.

Lorraine Harvey, 69, told The Sun: “When the work was going on one of our neighbours had a valuation of just over £1million.



“Then when she took the valuer out into the field he said ‘oh my god, if that gets any larger I’d knock £100,000 off the price’.

“Another house has only just sold after a long time… when a house goes on the market a drone goes up and captures that and it puts people off.

“Ours was on the market and the agent showed people around who got to the gate, saw the caravans and weren’t even interested in looking.

“Some of them have hot tubs and people are out there from early morning to late at night.

“I draw the curtains so I don’t have to see it, you shouldn’t have to draw the curtains in the summer.



“They keep saying they are working to the original plans but that is for a touring field for caravans and tents.

“We want them to remove the static caravans.”

Meadow Lakes Holiday Park has operated since 1979 as a camp site for tents and touring caravans.



But in January 2023, workmen rolled in with diggers, pulled up ancient hedgerows and cut down trees to make way for the luxury chalets.

When the work was going on Mrs Harvey went to speak to the operations manager who kept insisting they were working to “old plans”.

But she argues those plans were for 70 lodges on the north of the 56-acre site – much further away from their homes.

She contacted planning enforcement seven times in two months but said her pleas were ignored.



Bruce Bryan, 61, who has lived in Luney Barton for 32 years, compared the 60-caravan site to the “Blackpool Illuminations”.

He said: “The holiday park advertises online that they have this amazing site with a beautiful countryside view and all that rubbish.

“But that’s because they’re looking at my bloody house.

“What if we were to turn around and put 40 caravans in our field, they would be the first to go absolutely mental.

“It’s farcical, you can’t have one rule for them and another for everybody else.



“I am definitely using my garden less, I don’t use my hot tub any more, I don’t go out on my patio or have a barbecue.

“At night it’s all lit up like Blackpool illuminations.”

The park boasts amenities amenities such as four fishing lakes, a heated outdoor swimming pool and multiple play areas.

On its website, it is described as being “set within the beautiful Cornish countryside, with peaceful lakes that provide the perfect spot to relax”.

But Jane Collings, 56, slammed the site as an “eyesore” and accused it of negatively impacting house prices in the area.



And Jeff Harvey, 71, added: “It’s a huge blot on the landscape with no planning at all.

“We’re not against tourism but the whole principal of this is wrong.”

Meadow Lakes was purchased by Acorn Parks Ltd in 2009.

Addressing planning concerns, Rachel Nation, managing director of Acorn Parks, said the firm had “fully engaged” with the local authority.

She said: “Regarding the development in question and the concerns raised we have fully engaged with Cornwall Council providing all information that they requested from us over a period of over two years.



“We have also engaged with Grampound with Creed Parish Council and held a meeting at Meadow Lakes with some councillors from this parish council and also St Ewe Parish Council chairman and other councillors.

“I have also held a meeting with Lorraine and Jeff Harvey at Meadow Lakes and explained details about the development.

“I don’t have any specific knowledge of a plan shown to Lorraine Harvey by an ex-member of staff over three years ago, but Meadow Lakes has a long and detailed planning history.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A Cornwall Council spokesman said: “Extensive investigations have been carried out relating to this site.

“These have concluded that the siting of the caravans in their current location do not amount to breach of planning control.”

News.title: Andrew and Peter Mandelson are brutally mocked over Epstein links in SNL skit showing MI5 ‘decreasing his likeability’
News.content:
ROYAL ROAST Andrew and Peter Mandelson are brutally mocked over Epstein links in SNL skit showing MI5 ‘decreasing his likeability’

ANDREW Mountbatten-Windsor and Peter Mandelson have both been roasted in a comedy sketch, with fans calling it “genius”.

The pair were skewered in last night’s Saturday Night Live UK – with the former Duke of York, played by comedian Jack Shep, seen being ordered by MI5 to sully his own reputation in the wake of Princess Diana‘s death.





It comes as downcast Andrew was spotted yesterday watching his horses from behind a fence on the Sandringham estate after being banned from riding by royal aides.

They fear him being seen grinning on horseback is a “bad look” while under police investigation for allegedly leaking secrets to late paedo pal Jeffrey Epstein.

Epstein, Andrew and ex-British Ambassador to America, Mandelson, also accused of leaking sensitive information to the billionaire financier, were earlier this month all pictured lounging in an unearthed snap, in the first known photograph of the three together.

In the SNL sketch, agents hand the Andrew character a 29-year plan following the 1997 car crash tragedy which will see him and others close to the then-Prince Charles suffer a drop off in popularity to help “increase the likeability” of the future king.

Andrew, then in his 30s and still in active Royal Navy service, is seen in the skit – which opened the show – saying he is “willing to do whatever it takes”.

But on flicking through the dossier, he nervously asks whether all of it is necessary, including “befriending a notorious paedophile”, referring to his links to Epstein.

“Before and after he is convicted?” he continues. “And there is absolutely no other way to make my brother look good?”



Andrew then says he’s “sweating” at the prospect of carrying out some of the tasks, a reference to his infamous 2019 News Night interview in which he bizarrely claimed he was unable to perspire following his service in the Falklands.

He questions whether it’s possible to make “everyone around Charles unlikeable”, adding that Prince William is “so handsome”.

In a seemingly comedic dig at the now-Prince of Wales prematurely losing his hair, the agents tell him: “We’re seeing to that.”



Andrew is also told that Prince Harry will “marry a woman 98% of the UK public will find it impossible to have a normal conversation about”, in reference to Meghan Markle.

The Andrew character replies: “Goodness, this will kill Mummy when the news comes out.” They tell him: “Turn to page 72, it will.”

One agent then says “send in Agent Mandelson” before comedian Larry Dean emerges as Peter Mandelson, alongside fellow castmate Emma Sidi as Andrew’s ex-wife Sarah Ferguson.

The real Andrew and Mandelson were both arrested last month accused of passing sensitive information to Epstein while in a public office.



They were also mentioned, alongside Fergie, numerous times in the Epstein Files, a huge tranche of court documents, flight logs, emails and images relating to the late financier and being released in batches by the US Department of Justice.

In another reference to News Night during the SNL sketch, the agents tell Andrew: “Your Highness, if you’re ever in too deep, just say the code word and we’ll step in to save you.”

When he asks what that is, he’s told: “Pizza Express, Woking.”

Fans watching last night’s show hailed the Andrew sketch as “incredible”, with one writing: “I fear it’s already genius.”



Another said: “Oh god, perfect cold open on Andrew.”

The UK version of the long-running US-based SNL launched earlier this month, with last night’s second episode hosted by actor Jamie Dornan.

It comes as The Sun exclusively reported yesterday how the FBI investigated Andrew over claims he sought young girls for sex during a taxpayer-funded royal tour.



He is currently effectively housebound with just his dogs for company — including two of his late mother’s corgis.

Before moving to Sandringham in February, Andrew was regularly seen horse riding around the Windsor estate.

He was arrested on his birthday on February 19 on suspicion of misconduct in public office.

Police carried out searches of his new abode as well as previous home Royal Lodge at the time of his arrest.

Andrew allegedly passed sensitive emails to his paedophile financier pal Jeffrey Epstein while he was UK trade envoy.



Ex-British Ambassador to the US, Mandelson, meanwhile, was also arrested days later similarly accused of leaking sensitive government intelligence to Epstein.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Andrew has not commented on the allegation.

After his arrest, lawyers for Mandelson confirmed that police had removed all his bail conditions and his “overriding priority is to cooperate with the police investigation to clear his name”.

News.title: Police swarm Newcastle city centre street LIVE amid major emergency services response
News.content:

News.title: Harrowing moment hero neighbour tried to give stabbed girl, 16, CPR in Leeds murder probe
News.content:
EXCLUSIVE: Hero neighbours frantically try to save stabbed girl, 16, in Leeds murder probe

A teenage girl has died after she was discovered in a quiet residential street in the Crossgates area of Leeds, where she was bleeding from wounds to her back and neck

View 3 Images Teenage girl has died prompting a murder investigation by police. She has been named locally as Chloe Watson (Image: Facebook)

A man told how he desperately tried to save the life of a 16 year old girl who he believes had been stabbed in the back and neck.

‌



The 64 year old grandad gave CPR to the teen after she was found unconscious in his street but tragically she later died in hospital.

‌



A murder investigation has been launched following the death of the teenager in the early hours of Saturday morning. Three adults and one child have been arrested in connection with the incident.

‌



Police desperately tried to find the identity of the teenager, making a public appeal. Eventually they found out she lived with her mum and family in Cleckheaton, West Yorkshire, 16 miles and half an hour away from the crime scene.

View 3 Images The girl was found 'stabbed' in a quiet residential street (Image: Google)

On Sunday she was named locally as Chloe Watson, with friends paying tribute on social media, after her family had been contacted.

‌



Two grandfathers had tried to save Chloe, who they discovered wounded in their quiet street. Wayne Mallows, 64, described waking up at 5am, but had seen or heard nothing until a knock at his door 50 minutes later.

”I was called out of the house about 5.50am on Saturday morning by a dog walker. She said that my neighbour was outside doing CPR on a young girl.”

Mr Mallows said that his neighbour, who had been carrying out the CPR, lives across the street.

‌



The teenage girl was on the pavement directly opposite his neighbour's home on Kennerleigh Avenue, in the Crossgates area of East Leeds, which is now behind a police cordon.

Mr Mallows, speaking near the quiet street of bungalows with neat gardens, said he "went out" and could see his neighbour "was getting tired".

"I asked if they’d rung an ambulance and then I realised that a phone was on the ground and he had it on loud speaker. Ambulance control were giving him instructions.”

‌



Mr Mallows, who works in audiology for the NHS, said he’d received mandatory training in CPR on a mannequin, but never performed it in person.

"I took over until the ambulance arrived ten minutes later,” he said.

“She had been stabbed in the back and there was quite a bit of blood. Her eyes were just blank.” He also said there was a wound to her neck.

‌



“When the ambulance arrived around 6am the paramedics got all the kit out and tried to reactivate the heart and they were doing chest compressions,” he said.

View 3 Images West Yorkshire Police have launched a murder inquiry into the death of a 16 year old girl (Image: Getty Images/iStockphoto)

“They did that for about five minutes and then got her into the ambulance. Police were arriving all the time.”

‌



Despite the traumatic experience Mr Mallows said he is bearing up but is struggling to get the girl’s face out of his head. “In my mind I have a picture of her face,” said Mr Mallows. "To me she looked very young, younger than 16.:"

Mr Mallows confirmed that Kennerleigh Avenue and neighbouring streets are normally very quiet.

“It is mostly elderly people in the bungalows, they come here to retire,” he said.

‌



Officers said they were called at 5.55am on Saturday to the quiet residential area in Leeds, where she was found with serious injuries.

Initially West Yorkshire Police took the unusual step of releasing her description to ascertain her identity; describing her as a 5ft 2in slim woman aged in her late teens.

But now her friends and family have posted about their devastation and named her on social media, with one saying they were “heartbroken” and said she had so much love for her little sisters.

‌



Paying tribute to the teen, her pals wrote: “Your bubbly personality, your weird laugh, your cringy jokes will forever be unmatched. You always made sure everyone was feeling litty and loved…it’s truly devastating.”

Four people - two women aged 18, a man aged 20 and a 17-year-old boy - were all arrested from a nearby address on suspicion of murder and remain in custody, police said.

Detectives said on Sunday the girl has been positively identified as a 16-year-old from the Cleckheaton area. Her family have been notified and are now being supported by specially-trained officers.

‌



Senior investigating officer, Detective Chief Superintendent Marc Bowes, said: "Following our appeal for further information yesterday, we have now identified the deceased as a 16-year-old girl from the Cleckheaton area.

"Her family have been informed and we are supporting them as they try to come to terms with what has happened.

"Our inquiries into the incident which led to her death are continuing, and I would appeal again to anyone who was in the Kennerleigh Avenue area in the early hours of yesterday morning to come forward if they have any information which could assist our investigation."

Article continues below

Anyone with information is urged to call police on 101, or use the live chat options at westyorkshire.police.uk/livechat , quoting log 280 of March 28.

Information can also be given anonymously to Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111 or online.

News.title: KitKat heist of 400,000 bars sparks warning over chocolate shortage at Easter
News.content:
KitKat heist of 400,000 bars sparks warning over chocolate shortage at Easter

Thieves who stole more than 400,000 KitKat bars have sparked mayhem ahead of the Easter Bank Holiday Weekend, with the heist potentially leading to a shortage of the beloved chocolate on supermarket shelves

View 2 Images A KitKat spokesperson admits they approve of the 'criminals’ exceptional taste' (Stock Image) (Image: AP)

Mere days before Easter, and chocolate lovers have been dealt a very bitter blow indeed, with thieves pinching more than 400,000 KitKats from a truck in a brazen heist.

‌



The unsavoury crime unfolded in Switzerland, with the crooks targeting a truck as it made the journey from central Italy to Poland, distributing the much-loved bars along the route through Europe. To the dismay of chocoholics eagerly looking ahead to the Easter weekend, food and beverage giant Nestlé has warned that this "may lead to a shortage of KitKats appearing on shelves, which is why consumers, unfortunately, may struggle to find their favourite chocolates ahead of Easter."

‌



Meanwhile, a KitKat spokesperson this week quipped: “We’ve always encouraged people to have a break with KITKAT - but it seems thieves have taken the message too literally and made a break with more than 12 tonnes of our chocolate,"

‌



View 2 Images The crooks remain at large, while the chocolate is still unaccounted for (Stock Image) (Image: Bloomberg via Getty Images)

They continued: "Whilst we appreciate the criminals’ exceptional taste, the fact remains that cargo theft is an escalating issue for businesses of all sizes. With more sophisticated schemes being deployed on a regular basis, we have chosen to go public with our own experience in the hope that it raises awareness of an increasingly common criminal trend.”

‌



At the time of writing, the band of sweet-toothed highwaymen remain unaccounted for, as does their loot, and the vehicle in question. Nestlé has not shared exactly where the truck was lost. It's believed the stolen chocolate could well enter unofficial sales channels across Europe, but the company hasd not yet lost hope of tracking it down.

In a statement, KitKat revealed that the missing bars are, in fact, traceable using a unique batch code. Individuals who end up ⁠scanning these tell-tale batch numbers will be instructed on how to contact ⁠KitKat. According to Nestlé: "If a match is found, the scanner will be given clear instructions on how to alert KITKAT, who will then share the evidence appropriately."

This follows a joint report published just last month by the International Union of Marine Insurance and the Transported Asset Protection Association (TAPA) EMEA, outlining a worrying rise in cargo theft and freight fraud. With thieves using increasingly sophisticated ways to deceive. And it's feared that the dawn of AI will only ramp up the situation, which has already led to eyewatering financial losses.

Article continues below

According to this report, almost 160,000 cargo-related crimes were reported across 129 countries between 2022 and 2024, with total estimated losses reaching several billion Euros. Explaining the situation in a statement, Thorsten Neumann, President & CEO of TAPA EMEA, said: “Although conventional theft from trucks and warehouses is still prevalent, cargo crime is evolving. We are seeing criminals using digital tools to conceal their true identities, the creation of shell companies and legitimate firms being cloned using stolen credentials. Forged email addresses, look-alike domains and fake insurance certificates are increasingly common. Our concern is that artificial intelligence will accelerate these activities, making deception easier to scale and significantly driving up losses.”

News.title: Woman arrested after delivery driver and two cops allegedly assaulted in Walton
News.content:
Woman arrested after delivery driver and two cops allegedly assaulted in Walton

A 37-year-old woman has been arrested on suspicion of assault and two counts of assaulting emergency workers after an incident involving a delivery driver and police officers in Walton.

View 3 Images Police on Church Road West in Walton today (Image: Liverpool ECHO)

A woman has been arrested following assaults on a delivery driver and two police officers. Merseyside Police officers were in the County Road area of Walton this morning (Sunday) dealing with a separate investigation when they witnessed a delivery driver being attacked.

The force confirmed the incident was reported and uniformed officers in the vicinity attended the scene, arresting a woman on suspicion of assault. A force spokesperson said that following her caution, she "assaulted one of the officers and ran off".

However, as she fled, the woman tripped and caught her arm on a spiked, low metal fence surrounding the front door of a property on Church Road West. Merseyside Police said the woman allegedly went on to assault another officer who was attempting to administer first aid alongside a paramedic.

View 3 Images Police on Church Road West in Walton today (Image: Liverpool ECHO)

The 37-year-old woman was taken to the hospital, where she is currently receiving treatment for an arm injury, reports the Liverpool Echo. Alongside the initial assault allegation, she was further arrested on suspicion of two counts of assault on an emergency worker.

Residents on the street told the Echo the incident took place at around 11am. Upon arriving at the scene, the Echo found a small stretch of Church Road West cordoned off, covering approximately half a dozen houses on either side of the street.

Officers from two vehicles, including an unmarked car, were also present.

View 3 Images A police forensic officer on Church Road West in Walton today (Image: Liverpool ECHO)

Article continues below

A forensic officer from one of the force's scientific support units was conducting investigations on the pavement outside one of the properties.

One local resident told the Echo they became aware of the incident after they "heard shouting and screaming", adding that upon looking out of their front door they "saw someone lying on the ground in pain".

A second resident claimed they had been informed that "two women were on the floor wrestling", while a third reported witnessing a paramedic vehicle arrive at the scene.

News.title: Ryan Gosling's rare insight into family life as he shares young daughter's advice
News.content:
Ryan Gosling's rare insight into family life as he shares young daughter's advice

Having playing everything from a ­drug-addled teacher in Half Nelson to a bleached-blond Ken in Barbie, three-times Oscar nominee Ryan Gosling is now having a sci-fi moment

View 5 Images Ryan Gosling stars in new film, Project Hail Mary, which opened in the UK last week, and has taken £122million so far at the global box office, making it the biggest movie debut of the year. (Image: The Hollywood Reporter via Getty Images)

Renowned for the diversity of his roles, Ryan Gosling is currently starring in the box office smash Project Hail Mary, about an astronaut who befriends an alien in order to save both their planets, he is also appearing in Star Wars: Starfighter scheduled for release in May next year. But he thanks one of his daughters for the styling for Ryland Grace, the grade 8 science teacher reluctantly sent by the government to a star system 11.9 light years from Earth in Project Hail Mary – based on the novel by Andy Weir.

‌



He says: “I was playing around with the character and trying to put on stuff and I put on glasses as a joke almost, because it felt cliched to wear glasses to play a scientist. My daughter came by and she was like ‘You look smarter in glasses’. And I was like ‘Well, then, I’ll wear them’.” It certainly did no harm, as the film, which opened in the UK last week, has taken £122million so far at the global box office, making it the biggest movie debut of the year.

‌



Ryan, 45, who moved from California to Hampstead, North London, last year with Hitch actress Eva Mendes, 52, and their girls Esmeralda, 11, and Amada, nine, to film Starfighter, is a doting dad. He says his daughters help him “in so many ways, I couldn’t list them all”. The actor adds: “I think they’re so funny and helpful and smart.”

‌



View 5 Images Ryan Gosling as Ryland Grace in Project Hail Mary (Image: Amazon Content Services LLC/Jonathan Olley. All Rights Reserved)

Ryan and Eva, who met filming The Place Beyond the Pines in 2011, are believed to have married in a private ceremony in 2022. While the couple are keen to keep their children out of the spotlight, Ryan was thinking of them when he accepted the Project Hail Mary role. He says: “I was so grateful just as a father to get to make a story for my kids, maybe not to be too lofty, but for their generation. I was blown away by the book. I feel very lucky I got to have a unique experience, because it hadn’t been published yet, it was just in manuscript form, so I didn’t have any opinions to colour it for me.”

The Canadian actor’s impressive portfolio includes diverse roles such as a romantic hero in The Notebook, a jazz pianist in La La Land, a slick, sarcastic bond trader in The Big Short and an emotionally devastating performance as Dean Pereira in Blue Valentine. As Ryland Grace, he wakes up on an interstellar space craft with no memory of what has happened to him.

‌



Gradually it sinks in that he is the sole survivor of the crew and then that he is not alone – he is with an alien called Rocky, with whom he solves the scientific crisis. Heaping praise on author Andy Weir, Ryan says: “Partly what’s so special about Andy’s work is the humour, [which] helps you to digest so much of the hard science and some of the things that are harder to understand.”

5 View 5 Images Ryan Gosling with his wife, the actress Eva Mendes (Image: Getty Images) 5 View 5 Images Ryan won critical acclaim for his performance as Ken in the Barbie movie (Image: FILM STILL / HANDOUT)

‌



The cast brought their own take, he says. “It’s different because we had to personalise the humour and make it our own sense of humour. It became its own brand by the end of it.” Ryan loves that Ryland’s amnesia means he has no fixed idea of himself when he emerges from his cryogenic sleep.

He says: “I thought what was so compelling about him is that he doesn’t know who he is and that he’s not a natural hero. He has no fantasies of being a hero. He’s not like a typical movie hero, or he doesn’t want to be one. He finds his bravery in a really interesting way because he’s had amnesia and he’s able in a way to kind of forget who he was and that he might have been a coward. He’s given this opportunity to be who he wants to be and not who he was.”

Happy to praise the stagecraft, artistry and stunts that go into making top-class movies, Ryan recently revealed his disappoinment at missing a classic Tom Cruise moment during the filming of Starfighter – he was on a day off when the Mission: Impossible star swooped in by helicopter to direct a scene.

‌



View 5 Images On Project Hail Mary, Ryan has praised the incredible artistry employed to film the alien scenes. (Image: AP)

Ryan says: “Tom Cruise flew his helicopter on to set. They were just shooting, and they heard a helicopter, they had to cut. And it was Tom Cruise. He lands in the middle of the set. He takes a camera, and he just starts shooting the action scene. It was an incredible moment, and I don’t know why he waited for the one day I wasn’t there. I’m gonna hope that was an accident.”

Meanwhile, on Project Hail Mary, he praises the incredible artistry employed to film the alien scenes. He says: “It is puppetry and I think that’s the secret sauce of the movie. It really would have been a lot easier and a lot cheaper to do it another way. It was quite difficult to do it this way. I mean, five, six puppeteers. All of that entails having it work properly on camera. Creating space in the set for all of that was not something I think we anticipated. I don’t think anyone told our production designer that the set didn’t actually have to function in space!”

Article continues below

And the difficulty of bringing Rocky the alien to life, in turn, reflected the complications of the relationship between the extra-terrestrial and the reluctant astronaut, its human companion. Ryan says: “They can’t be in each other’s atmosphere. They can’t communicate. Everything is difficult, and we were living that on set.” But they achieved a fantastic result and, as Ryan concludes: “It all became part of the magic of the film."

*This interview was adapted from The Arts Hour on the BBC World Service. It can be heard in its entirety on BBC Sounds.

News.title: Man jailed after taping wedding ring to car sun visor and going to meet 'girl, 12'
News.content:
Man jailed after taping wedding ring to car sun visor and going to meet 'girl, 12'

Alan Williams, 57, travelled from Cheshire to Hull after exchanging messages with what he thought was a 12-year-old girl

View Image Alan Williams was jailed for a year at Hull Crown Court (Image: Humberside Police)

An online sexual predator made a two-hour journey to Hull – leaving his wedding ring in his vehicle – to meet a 12-year-old girl he "fancied" after exchanging explicit messages with her.

‌



Alan Williams purchased a 24-hour parking ticket and went to a cafe near the railway station - but was stunned when police suddenly turned up to arrest him, Hull Live reported. The "pretty" girl he was so keen to meet was actually a decoy set up to catch people like him, Hull Crown Court heard.

‌



Williams, 57, pleaded guilty to attempting to engage in sexual communication with a child under 16 between May 10 and 28 last year and attempting to meet a girl under 16 following grooming on May 28 last year. Billy Torbett, prosecuting, said that Williams exchanged messages online with a decoy 12-year-old girl on Snapchat.

‌



He sent her a friend request and she told him that she was 12 and from Hull. Williams asked for pictures of her and told her that she was "pretty" and "gorgeous" and he asked her if she would meet him if he travelled to Hull from Manchester.

He told her that she was his "little girl" and that he would take her to a hot tub and drink with her when she was 16. They planned to rendezvous at Hull railway station but, on the day, he informed her that a family emergency prevented him from visiting.

He later requested a full body photo of the girl and proposed they meet the following Friday for bowling and a meal. He confessed to her that he "fancied" her and called her "gorgeous".

‌



They scheduled to meet at Hull railway station on May 28 and Williams journeyed two hours from Cheshire to see her. That morning, he messaged the decoy girl to say he was in Hull and waiting outside Caffè Nero, near the train station. Police arrived there at 9.08am and Williams was apprehended.

"He was observed by officers to be pacing outside Caffè Nero," said Mr Torbett. "His vehicle was found parked near the location. He had a 24-hour parking ticket."

A wedding ring was attached to the visor of the car.

‌



"It was the defendant's wedding ring that he had taken off," Mr Torbett explained. "He is married."

During his police interview, Williams remained silent in response to all questions. He had no prior convictions.

Rachel Scott, defending, stated that Williams pleaded guilty ahead of a planned trial date. He initially denied the charges but later altered his pleas.

‌



"He makes no excuses for his behaviour," Miss Scott declared. "He is thoroughly embarrassed and ashamed of his behaviour. He is devastated and disgusted at his own actions.

"He has denied any sexual interest in children. He has taken steps to address his behaviour. He has no social media accounts at all now.

"He feels like this is really rock bottom for him. He has shown genuine remorse."

‌



Williams had been employed by an air conditioning firm, working across the country.

Judge John Thackray KC told Williams: "You made contact with what you thought was a 12-year-old girl via Snapchat. You made a friend request and in full knowledge or expectation that you were speaking or communicating with a 12-year-old girl.

"You requested images, you told her that she was pretty, that she was gorgeous, that you fancied her. You travelled over two hours intending to meet a 12-year-old girl.

Article continues below

"The offence is so serious that only a custodial sentence can be justified. The seriousness of the offence means that appropriate punishment can only be achieved by way of an immediate custodial sentence."

Williams, of Ullswater Terrace, Stalybridge, Tameside, Greater Manchester, was imprisoned for one year.

He was handed a seven-year sexual harm prevention order and must register as a sex offender for 10 years. Williams, who had been on bail, must pay a £187 victims' surcharge.

News.title: Horror crash kills three including girl, 13, as car hits tree near Garthorpe
News.content:
Horror crash kills three including girl, 13, as car hits tree near Garthorpe

Humberside Police are appealing for witnesses after a white Audi TT left the road and collided with a tree

View Image Police say a white Audi TT left the road and ploughed into a tree near Garthorpe (Image: Google Maps)

A 13-year-old girl and two men in their 40s have died following a crash near the village of Garthorpe on Saturday evening. Humberside Police have launched an investigation after a white Audi TT, travelling southbound along Shore Road between Garthorpe and Meredyke Road, veered off the road and struck a tree.

The incident is believed to have occurred at around 5:45pm, with officers yet to establish why the vehicle left the road. Emergency services were swiftly dispatched to the scene, where the driver, a 44-year-old man, the front seat passenger, a 48-year-old man, and one of the rear seat passengers, a 13-year-old girl, were all pronounced dead at the scene, reports Grimsby Live.

A nine-year-old boy and a 15-year-old girl were rushed to the hospital with serious injuries. In a statement, Humberside Police confirmed that the girl's injuries are life-threatening and that she remains in a critical condition.

Article continues below

The families of those who died have been informed and are receiving support from specially trained officers.

Police are now working to piece together the full circumstances of the crash. They are urging anyone who witnessed the collision, or who holds any relevant information including CCTV or dashcam footage from around the time of the incident, to get in touch via Humberside Police's non-emergency number 101, quoting log 422 of 28 March.

News.title: Tributes paid to 'beautiful, bubbly girl' who died in Leeds as murder probe launched
News.content:
Tributes paid to 'beautiful, bubbly girl' who died in Leeds as murder probe launched

Tributes have poured in for a 16-year-old girl who died after being found with serious injuries in a street in Leeds - she has been named locally as Chloe Watson and remembered as a 'beautiful girl' with a 'bubbly personality'

View 2 Images Chloe Watson has been named locally as the 16-year-old girl who died after an incident in Austhorpe, Leeds (Image: Facebook)

Tributes have poured in for a 16-year-old girl who died after being found with serious injuries.

‌



The teenager - whose death is being investigated by police as a murder - has been named locally as Chloe Watson. Officers were called at 5.55am on Saturday to Kennerleigh Avenue in Austhorpe, Leeds, to reports that a young woman had been found unconscious, West Yorkshire Police said. She suffered serious injuries and was taken to hospital, where she was sadly pronounced dead shortly afterwards, the force said.

‌



Public tributes posted to Facebook have expressed the community's "heartbreak" over the death of the 16-year-old, Leeds Live reports. One post read: "I am going to miss you, Chloe Watson. Sending love to your family, looking over everyone, especially your little sisters - you had so much love for them. Love you millions, my girl."

‌



View 2 Images Police have launched a murder investigation (Image: Facebook)

Another tribute read: "Rest in peace, you beautiful girl, you are so loved and will continue to be loved forever. You will be forever missed and never forgotten. Your bubbly personality, your weird laugh, and your cringy jokes will forever be unmatched. You always made sure everyone was feeling loved, and we will continue to do that for you."

‌



Two 18-year-old women, a 20-year-old man and a 17-year-old boy were arrested on suspicion of murder on Saturday. All four remain in police custody while a crime scene is in place as officers carry out enquiries.

Detectives were not immediately able to identify the teenager, but they said on Sunday that she was a 16-year-old girl from the Cleckheaton area. Her family have been notified and are being supported by specially trained officers.

Senior investigating officer Detective Chief Superintendent Marc Bowes said: "Following our appeal for further information yesterday, we have now identified the deceased as a 16-year-old girl from the Cleckheaton area. Her family have been informed and we are supporting them as they try to come to terms with what has happened.

Article continues below

"Our inquiries into the incident which led to her death are continuing, and I would appeal again to anyone who was in the Kennerleigh Avenue area in the early hours of yesterday morning to come forward if they have any information which could assist our investigation."

Anyone with information is asked to contact police by calling 101 or using the online live chat function, quoting log number 280 of March 28. Information can also be passed anonymously to the independent charity Crimestoppers by calling 0800 555 111 or visiting the Crimestoppers website.

News.title: Jeremy Bowen: Trump is waging war based on instinct and it isn't working
News.content: Unless both sides can make a giant leap into an unexplored middle ground of compromise, it is hard to see a deal being made. It is not impossible. The Iranian regime has a history of negotiation. Arab diplomatic sources have backed up other reports, telling me that Iran was offering a path towards a deal on its nuclear programme when the US abruptly abandoned diplomacy by going to war on 28 February. One source told me: "You know the Iranians were offering everything." That sounds like an over-simplification, and the Americans deny progress was being made, but the signs are there was room for more diplomacy when the US and Israel sent in bombers.

News.title: Tudor leaves Spurs after just 44 days in charge
News.content:
Igor Tudor has left his role as Tottenham Hotspur interim head coach after just 44 days and seven matches.

Spurs said they have "mutually agreed" with the Croat to part ways with "immediate effect".

The decision comes a week after a damaging 3-0 home defeat by fellow strugglers Nottingham Forest on 22 March - a result that left Spurs 17th in the table and only one point above the relegation places with seven games remaining.

Tottenham have suffered five defeats in seven matches in all competitions since Tudor succeeded the sacked Thomas Frank on 14 February, on a deal until the end of the season.

Spurs said: "An update on a new head coach will be provided in due course."

BBC Sport understands Spurs will appoint Tudor's replacement in the next few days to be in place for when most players return from international duty.

Tudor's assistant Bruno Saltor will oversee training for those at the club.

They confirmed goalkeeping coach Tomislav Rogic and physical coach Riccardo Ragnacci have also departed.

Tudor, 47, did not undertake post-match media duties after the defeat by Forest because of the death of his father.

"We thank Igor, Tomislav and Riccardo for their efforts during the past six weeks, in which they worked tirelessly," said Spurs in a statement.

"We also acknowledge the bereavement that Igor has recently suffered and send our support to him and his family at this difficult time."

News.title: What can F1's bosses do to help keep Verstappen in the sport?
News.content:
Max Verstappen said after the Japanese Grand Prix that he was considering quitting Formula 1 - but the sport's bosses "know what to do" to keep him in it.

Verstappen's issue is with the new rules. He has been clear all year that the new form of driving and racing the new hybrid engines have created is not to his taste. And he repeated that opinion after the race in Suzuka, as well as before it.

The four-time champion said he was "not enjoying the whole formula behind it, it doesn't feel natural to a racing driver".

He added: "Of course I try to adapt to it, but it's not nice the way you have to race. It's really anti-driving. Then at one point, yeah, it's just not what I want to do."

Verstappen made it clear in the interview with BBC Sport in which he made his powerful remarks that his opinion was not based on his lack of competitiveness this season as his Red Bull team struggle.

That will be bad news for Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies, who said he and Verstappen were "focusing on the competitive picture" and "having zero discussions about the other aspects".

Mekies added: "I'm sure by the time we give him a fast car, he will be a much happier Max. And by the time we give him a car he can push and make the difference with, he will also be a happier Max."

Verstappen is the most outspoken of the drivers about the new rules, but is far from the only one unhappy. Most of the drivers have misgivings on one level or another.

Before Japan, the general consensus among F1 bosses seemed to be that the new power-units and their 50-50 split between internal combustion and electrical power, and consequent focus on energy management, had had a beneficial impact on racing.

But it was accepted they have a detrimental effect on qualifying - where the drivers have almost universally complained of a diminished challenge in some of the sport's fastest corners, as they have to take them at lower speeds because of the need to recover energy.

However, the Japanese race highlighted a problem about which drivers have been warning in racing, too.

Haas' Oliver Bearman had a frightening high-speed crash at Spoon Curve, caused by a 50km/h speed differential between his car and Franco Colapinto's Alpine.
